source_name: IN516HT d.o.o. — analytics partner site
why_relevant: Slovenian analytics/BI and planning consultancy whose public client examples include financial-sector names (e.g. Modra zavarovalnica). Analytics/planning is a growing bank spend category and this vendor publishes client work, which reveals the underlying BI platforms (and therefore the foreign vendors) used in SI financial institutions.

source_name: COMLAND d.o.o. — company record (razvoj informacijskih rešitev)
why_relevant: Long-established (1991) Slovenian software-development house, ~33 employees, Cesta Ljubljanske brigade 21, Ljubljana. Actor-map entry for the domestic supplier landscape; registry record is the reliable anchor since the vendor site did not surface in search.

source_name: Endava digitalne rešitve d.o.o. (Ljubljana) — D&B company profile
why_relevant: Establishes the Slovenian Endava entity (Letališka cesta 29B, Ljubljana; ~231 employees at the location, ~USD 36m reported sales). Endava globally is a banking/payments delivery partner, so its Slovenian delivery centre is a channel through which foreign payments platforms reach the region. The SI unit publishes no client list, so the entity profile plus the global site is the practical tracking route.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — ZBS B2B programska orodja
why_relevant: The Slovenian Banking Association's B2B page covers shared software tooling/standards used across member banks. Because the association coordinates cross-bank technical schemes, its pages and documents point to which vendors and standards the whole SI banking sector has adopted — a pointer into vendor relationships that individual banks do not disclose.

source_name: GZS — Združenje za informatiko in telekomunikacije (ZIT): KATALOGI
why_relevant: The Chamber of Commerce ICT association publishes member catalogues, an ICT reference price list and event programmes. This is the systematic way to enumerate Slovenian IT houses (including those selling into banks) rather than discovering them one brand at a time — the canonical actor-list pointer for this cell.

source_name: Računalniške novice — partner/vendor profile pages (SI IT trade media)
why_relevant: Slovenian IT trade outlet hosting per-vendor partner profile pages and vendor news. Useful both as a directory of active SI IT houses and as a place where vendors announce bank projects that never appear in English-language media.

source_name: Finance.si IKT-informator (sponsored ICT supplements)
why_relevant: Finance's periodic IKT-informator supplement is where Slovenian IT houses buy space to describe their solutions and name clients, including financial-sector ones. Copies are frequently re-hosted on vendor sites (as here on Mikrografija's), so the supplements are collectable even without a Finance subscription. Good longitudinal record of vendor positioning.

source_name: SloExport — Slovenian exporters directory (company cards)
why_relevant: Official-adjacent directory of Slovenian exporting companies with structured company cards (activity, products, markets). Useful for identifying which domestic IT houses actually export banking software beyond SI — i.e. which ones are genuine regional competitors rather than local-only integrators.

source_name: Marand d.o.o. — corporate site (actor-map entry, banking relevance unconfirmed)
why_relevant: Named in the cell brief as a domestic IT house. Two searches (sl and en) returned no evidence of Slovenian banking references for Marand — the visible public footprint is engineering/health informatics (openEHR) rather than banking. Listed at low priority as an actor to check directly rather than as an evidenced banking source; the URL is the conventional corporate domain and is provided unverified.

source_name: Bankart — Aktualno (news / press releases)
why_relevant: Running feed of partnership announcements, leadership changes and product launches — the closest thing to a Bankart press-release wire. Observed items include the 2025 CEO change (Samo Kumar succeeding Aleksandar Kurtevski) and a 2026 CTO appointment.

source_name: Bankart — English site
why_relevant: English mirror used for regional/international positioning; useful for extracting comparable claims (client-bank counts, countries served) that are phrased more explicitly than in the SL pages.

source_name: Bankart — 'Opis placilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij' (PDF)
why_relevant: Formal scheme documentation describing SIMP-PS and BIPS operation, participant roles and governance (e.g. SIMP committee composition). High-density technical/structural source naming system participants and rules.

source_name: Flik — official scheme site (flik.si)
why_relevant: National instant-payment scheme site; repeatedly cited by Bankart and by banks as the canonical location of the list of banks supporting Flik Pay / Flik POS / Flik e-commerce. That participant list is a direct pointer to every SI bank in the instant-payments graph.

source_name: Bankart — Flik product pages (Pay / POS / e-commerce)
why_relevant: Product-level detail on the Flik family operated by Bankart, including FAQ pages that name supporting banks, acceptance channels and merchant onboarding routes — useful for mapping who resells/integrates Flik.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nadzor nebancnih ponudnikov placilnih storitev in infrastruktur financnega trga
why_relevant: Explains the oversight perimeter over non-bank PSPs and FMIs and links onward to authorisations, reporting instructions and oversight outputs — the regulatory scaffolding that determines which vendors must be publicly registered.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Placilna infrastruktura / placilni sistemi (BIPS, SIMP-PS, TARGET)
why_relevant: Central bank description of each national rail: BIPS (instant payments, established 2019, operated at Bankart), SIMP-PS, TARGET2-Slovenija. Names the operator/participant structure and is the reference for how Bankart-run rails sit relative to Eurosystem rails.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Nacionalni svet za placila (National Payments Council) materials
why_relevant: Meeting materials of the national payments forum. Search snippets show agenda items such as progress reports on building the instant-payments infrastructure at Bankart (BIPS) — i.e. roadmap-level intelligence on national rails and the vendors behind them, published in advance of press coverage.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — Porocilo o placilnih in poravnalnih sistemih (annual payment & settlement systems report)
why_relevant: Annual oversight report on SI payment and settlement systems; a 2021 edition was found mirrored on findinfo.si. Gives volumes, participant counts and system-by-system commentary — the quantitative backbone for sizing Bankart-run rails.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — SISBON (central credit register, individuals)
why_relevant: Banka Slovenije is the confirmed operator (upravljavec) of SISBON under ZCKR-1. Pages cover system rules, member creditors and the 'Moj SISBON' mobile app — the app itself implies an IT delivery relationship worth tracing as a vendor lead.

source_name: Banka Slovenije — SISBIZ (central credit register, legal entities) incl. dedicated portal
why_relevant: SISBIZ is operated by Banka Slovenije under ZCKR-1 and has its own portal (vsebina.bsi.si/sisbiz) with an 'Organiziranost' page describing governance and reporting members — i.e. a named list of participating creditors, a pointer into the lender/vendor graph.

source_name: KDD — Centralna klirinsko depotna druzba (CSD / settlement system operator)
why_relevant: Slovenia's CSD and settlement-system operator, T2S-connected since 2017, supervised by ATVP and Banka Slovenije. Its Pravila poslovanja (rulebook PDFs) define system membership; membership implies a publishable participant list — dense pointer to the post-trade actor set.

source_name: ATVP — Securities Market Agency page on KDD
why_relevant: Supervisor-side description of KDD and of 'udelezenci na financnem trgu' — a regulator-curated taxonomy of financial-market participants, useful for validating actor names and catching authorisation changes.

source_name: Zdruzenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — payment operations section and news
why_relevant: Bank association acting as a de-facto standards body for SI payments: publishes the open ZBSxml data-exchange standard, tool listings ('Programska orodja'), member-bank roster and press releases. Standards pages point directly at the software vendors implementing them.

source_name: UJP — Uprava RS za javna placila (public-sector payments operator) and its service portal
why_relevant: State operator of public-sector payment traffic, the budget-user register (iRPU) and e-invoicing (UJPnet / eRacun). It is both a rail operator adjacent to Bankart and a large public buyer of payments technology; its B2B integration specs name the vendors that connect to it.

source_name: ERAR (KPK) — public money-flow transparency application
why_relevant: Publishes transaction flows between public-sector entities and private companies under ZIntPK arts. 75a/75b. Lets you observe payments from public bodies (incl. central-bank-adjacent and state buyers) to payments vendors — a quantitative supplier-relationship signal not available elsewhere.

source_name: Vendor case-study pages naming Bankart (IBM, Nets/Nexi, fintech trade press)
why_relevant: Bankart is a buyer of vendor technology; suppliers publish the relationship when Bankart will not. IBM hosts a Bankart case study, and FinTech Futures reported a Bankart–Nets deal to deliver new payments infrastructure to the Slovenian banking sector. This class of page is the single best evidence of Bankart's technology stack and supplier set.

source_name: Rekono–Bankart partnership announcement (identity/trust services)
why_relevant: Concrete, dated example of Bankart signing a technology partnership (remote identification and e-transaction trust services with Rekono). Template case for how Bankart partnerships surface — via its own site rather than the partner's — and a lead into the SI eID/trust-service vendor cluster.
